Well, yeah, it definitely has an impact, though I guess I'm still functioning on some level. Well... prevent me from doing anything at all? I mean, I guess it depends on what you mean by "anything." Like, I don't think I've ever just laid in bed for three days straight completely unable to move a muscle, if that's what you're asking. But there are definitely these moments... these really weird, frustrating moments where I just get so overwhelmed by everything—the sadness, the heavy feeling, the restless energy—that my brain just kind of short-circuits, I guess? 

Like, the other morning, I was trying to get ready for work, and I was already running late because it took me forever just to put my shoes on. Just frozen. I wasn't thinking about anything specific, I wasn't daydreaming... I was just stuck there for I don't know how long. Maybe a minute? Maybe five? It felt like my body just forgot what it was supposed to do next. 

And then, on the flip side, when the restlessness gets really bad, I do this thing where I just walk the same little loop by the couch over and over again. Like, from the armrest, around the coffee table, back to the armrest. Just pacing that same tiny circle for no real reason. I'm not looking for anything, I'm not trying to get anywhere... I'm just doing it. And while I'm doing it, I'm not getting anything else done. I'm not answering emails, I'm not making breakfast, I'm just... stuck in that loop. So, I guess in those moments, yeah, it completely prevents me from doing what I'm actually supposed to be doing. It's like my body is doing something, but *I'm* not really doing anything, if that makes sense. It's just so bizarre, and it eats up so much time that I don't really have to spare right now.

Yeah, it’s definitely been longer than two weeks. Honestly, it feels like it's been going on for a couple of months now, just this heavy, blank feeling that won't lift. You know, I used to have all these little things that made up my week, things that really made me feel like myself outside of work. Like, I’ve always been really into sketching. I’d go to different local cafes and write down these detailed little coffee notes in a separate journal, comparing the different roasts, trying to pick out if it tasted like blueberry or cocoa or whatever. Those were the things that kept me grounded and made me feel alive. 

But lately... I just don't care about any of it. I'll literally sit at my kitchen table, open the sketchbook, uncap my pen, and I just... I just feel nothing pulling me toward it. I'll just stare at the blank page and feel completely empty. Or I'll force myself to sit on the edge of my bed on a Saturday morning and lace up my hiking boots because I know I *should* go outside, but then I just sit there. There's no spark, no motivation, no interest at all. It’s like the part of my brain that used to get excited about a new trail or a good cup of coffee just completely shut off. So I usually just end up untying the boots, taking them back off, and going back to doing absolutely nothing.

Anyone would, right? But it's just a passing thing. It definitely doesn't last for a week straight. If anything, my problem right now is the exact opposite of everything you just asked about. I'm just so flat. The idea of having enough energy to be extremely happy, or to be that fired up and irritable about something for days on end... it honestly just sounds exhausting to even picture. I just don't have that kind of spark in me. I've always been pretty even-keeled, maybe a little on the quiet side, but never these huge, extended highs you're talking about. It's just never happened.

No, I can't say I've ever experienced anything like that. Honestly, the idea of having a lot of energy without getting much sleep sounds like something out of a sci-fi movie to me. I mean, sleep is... well, it's a whole thing for me right now, but it's definitely not because I have all this extra energy to burn.

And lately, with everything feeling so heavy and blank, sleep is basically the only thing I *want* to do. It's not that I'm waking up at 3 AM feeling refreshed and ready to go for a run or clean the whole apartment. If I'm awake in the middle of the night, it's just because I'm lying there staring at the ceiling, feeling that weird restless energy I mentioned earlier, but it's not a *productive* energy. Like, my sister pointed it out, and it made me realize how bad it's gotten. \n\nWhen the slowness hits, it's a very specific, heavy feeling. I'm literally moving like I'm underwater. It takes me forever just to answer a simple question or even push myself up out of a chair. It's like gravity has suddenly doubled in the room just for me. And then, completely out of nowhere, it switches. I'll get this restless phase where I'm just pacing back and forth across my apartment. My living room isn't even that big, but I'll just walk from the window to the kitchen counter, over and over, and I'll be rubbing my hands together constantly. It feels exactly like I'm trying to physically shake off the stress of a really awful customer service call—you know, when someone screams at you for twenty minutes about a late fee—but there's no call. It's just my body doing it. So they definitely feel like these intense, separate phases of either being totally weighed down or completely wired, even if they happen on the same day.\n\nDoctor: Do you notice any difference in your mood when you're experiencing one of these episodes of slowness versus when you're feeling restless?\n\nPatient: I... well, I know I touched on this a little bit before, but... honestly, no, I don't really notice a difference in my mood between the two. It's not like... it's not like when I'm slow, I'm sad, and when I'm pacing, I'm angry or anxious or anything like that. I mean, I *am* anxious sometimes, but the mood itself, that heavy, gray sadness I was talking about? It just kind of stays there. It's like the background noise to everything else. \n\nWhether I'm sitting at my desk, staring at the screen for ten minutes trying to figure out how to type a simple email because my fingers feel like they're made of lead, or if I'm up and pacing around the living room, rubbing my hands together until they're red... the sadness is just there. I just haven't noticed any kind of shift in how I feel emotionally when those physical things are happening. It's all just one big, continuous slump.\n\nDoctor: Are you having trouble keeping up with work or maintaining relationships with family and friends because of these episodes of slowness and restlessness?\n\nPatient: Well, yeah, it definitely has an impact, though I guess I'm still functioning on some level. Like, my routines... making meals, running errands... it all just slides unless I absolutely force myself to do it. I just haven't noticed any kind of shift in how I feel emotionally when those physical things are happening. No, no, I... I feel like we're sort of circling around the same thing here, honestly. Like I was saying with the sleep and the energy before... I've never had a time where I felt extremely happy, or, you know, on top of the world, and just didn't need to sleep. That whole combination just doesn't happen for me.

Sleep has always been this fixed point for me. My body demands it. If I don't get it, I'm useless. So the idea of being so happy or so irritable that I just bypass the need for sleep entirely... it's just so far removed from anything I've ever experienced. I really can't emphasize enough how much I've always needed my sleep, and how right now, it's pretty much the only escape I have, even if it's broken up by lying there staring at the ceiling.
